newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fourth victim dies in S.African bomb blasts.
newsitem.headline: Fourth victim dies in S.African bomb blasts.

text.p: The twin Christmas Eve bombs, which killed three people and wounded about 60 in a small South African town, claimed the life of another child on Tuesday, state radio reported.
The pipe bombs sprayed shrapnel into crowds of Christmas shoppers at a supermarket and a pharmacy in the town of Worcester, about 90 km (55 miles) northeast of Cape Town.

The third child to die, Andile Matshoba, 13, -- whose younger brother Xolani was also killed in the blast -- died in hospital after being kept alive on machines. He was declared brain dead on Tuesday morning.

Police said last week the detonation of the bombs within seconds of each other could indicate a conspiracy involving several perpetrators, including unspecified political motives, gang violence, or the work of vigilantes.
But Justice Minister Dullah Omar said the bombings might have been carried out by a criminal gang seeking revenge for the arrest of its members.

He said criminals had been apprehended in the store a week previously, and speculated it could therefore be the work of the syndicate or criminal gang whose men had been arrested and denied bail in court.
No one has claimed responsibility for the attacks.
Police offered a reward of half a million rand ($107,000) for information and are still hunting three men seen fleeing the town after the bombs went off.
